quote:
A weary ceasefire, like a patient resting on a fragile bridge, must be nurtured or it will be swept away by winds of old grievances.  

When a hidden virus whispers through valleys, the wise judge that few hold yet many fear.  

When ink runs thin, a banner may switch to monochrome, reminding the world that darkness can be the stillness before the dawn.  

In the bowing fields of Kenya, a land once bound to a distant master now offers seeds of a new garden to those who once tilled its soil.  

Two great winds that rise together may either become gentle breezes or stormy torrents; the choice lies in the hearts that convene.  

Where walls of violence are erected, the echo of lost children resounds louder than armor; the true path lies in binding rather than burning.  

When the earth sacks itself with excess, the future bears the weight of the famine in its pockets; humility is the seed that will grow into abundance.
